description: One measure over many files as one tidy table, optionally joined to sample sheets or plate maps (the join key is chosen from the data and reported in joins[] with unmatched rows) and summarized by group (by; test against a control). Analyses (peaks, chromatogram, nmr-peaks, ephys-features, spikes, qpcr, gate, assay) take the arguments of their tools as options. Inputs (paths): files, directories, globs or an index query. Returns at most limit rows (page with offset; output writes them all to a file); a failing file is a row with error. openreadout_summarize regroups a table written by an earlier output.

by.description: Summarize by these columns (e.g. `["condition"]`): n, mean, sd, sem, median, min, max, cv_percent per group; channels/parameters/populations stay apart automatically.

exact_by.description: Group by exactly `by` (do not add the measurement columns that vary).

fields.description: Columns to keep (info: index field names, or `["all"]`).

from_index.description: Also take the data sets an index query selects: the index directory …

keys.description: Fixed join keys `SHEET_COLUMN=FIELD` (path, file, stem, sample_id, sample_name, barcode, well, position, run_order, column:NAME).

limit.description: Rows to return (default 20, max 500; 0 with `output`: the rows are in the file).

measure.description: What to measure per data set. `stats` = pixel statistics per image × channel (per=well for screening plates); `trace` = statistics per trace × sweep × channel; `table` = FCS: events, median, mean, sd, min, max per parameter; plate reads: one row per well; `info` = one row of header metadata per data set (fields); `scans` = one row per MS scan header (options: the openreadout_scans filters); `peaks` = openreadout_peaks (its arguments as options); `chromatogram` = openreadout_chromatogram (its arguments as options); `assay` = a plate-reader assay: options `analysis` (wells, curve, dose-response, kinetics, growth, qc) and the other openreadout_assay arguments; `nmr-peaks` = openreadout_nmr_peaks (its arguments as options); `ephys-features` = openreadout_ephys_features (its arguments as options); `spikes` = openreadout_spikes (its arguments as options); `qpcr` = openreadout_qpcr (its arguments as options); `gate` = population counts, percentages and medians (workspace or gatingml).

options.description: The measure's options. Analyses: the arguments of that analysis's tool (openreadout_peaks, openreadout_nmr_peaks, openreadout_assay with its `analysis`, ...), plus `rows` (which record list becomes rows: peaks peak|compound|chromatogram|band|region, nmr-peaks peak|integral|spectrum, ephys-features sweep|cell|spike, qpcr record|rq|standard_curve, assay wells|samples|compounds|kinetics|growth|quality). stats: image, select, level, per (channel|image|plane|well|field), wells, mip (z|t). trace: trace, sweep, channels. table: table, parameters, compensate, transform, workspace or gatingml, sample. gate: workspace or gatingml, sample, populations, medians, table. info: fields. scans: the openreadout_scans filters.

output.description: Write the full table (or the summary, with `by`) to this .csv/.tsv/.jsonl/.json/.parquet file (verified; never overwrites without `overwrite`).

query.description: … and the query (search syntax, e.g. "format=fcs channel~CD4").

replicate.description: Average rows within each replicate first.

sample_sheets.description: Sample sheets (CSV/TSV/XLSX) or plate layouts (plate-map grids) to join; the key is chosen from the data (file name, path, sample id recorded in the file, well, barcode, vial, run order) and reported under joins[].

test.description: `welch` or `mann-whitney` against `control` (a value of the first `by` column).

values.description: Value columns to summarize (default: the measure's main values).

name: openreadout_batch

name.description: Name (stable; units that never change are part of it, e.g. `sample_rate_hz`).

unit.description: Unit of every value in the column, when fixed.

ColumnType.description: Column type, inferred from the cells.

oneOf.description: Text.
Whole numbers.
Real numbers (a column mixing integers and reals is `float`).
`true`/`false`.

InputReport.description: How the inputs turned into data sets.

datasets.description: Data sets measured (rows come from these), including those that failed.

failed.description: Data sets that failed (their rows carry `error`).

grouped_members.description: Files that belong to another input's multi-file data set (measured once, with it).

reused.description: Data sets whose rows were reused from the journal of an interrupted run.

skipped_examples.description: A few of the skipped paths, with why.

skipped_format.description: Data sets of other formats left out by the format filter.

skipped_sheets.description: Sample sheets and layouts found among the inputs (never measured).

skipped_unknown.description: Files found by walking a directory that no reader recognises (not in the table).

alternatives.description: The next best keys (auto only), to judge how clear the choice was.

ambiguous.description:
Table rows that matched several sheet rows that disagree (first 20); left without
annotations.

auto.description: True when the key was chosen from the data (no `--key`).

key.description: The key used: one or more (sheet column, field) pairs, all of which must agree.

matched_datasets.description: Data sets with at least one annotated row.

unmatched_datasets.description: Data sets no sheet row matched (first 20).

unmatched_datasets_count.description: How many data sets no sheet row matched.

unmatched_sheet_rows.description: Sheet rows that matched no table row, by their key values (first 20).

unmatched_sheet_rows_count.description: How many sheet rows matched nothing.

KeyField.description: A key of the table's rows a sheet column can match.

oneOf.description: The data set's path relative to its input (or any trailing part of it).
The file name with its extension.
The file name without its extension(s) (or with them: `a` and `a.fcs` both match).
`experiment.sample.id`.
`experiment.sample.name`.
`experiment.sample.barcode` (plate or tube barcode).
The row's plate well (`well` column, else `experiment.sample.well`).
`experiment.sample.sequence_position` (vial, autosampler position).
1-based rank of the data set's acquisition start time.
Any column of the table (`column:<name>` on the command line).
Which data set a row comes from: `path`, `format`, `files`.

The row's position within its data set (the measure's grain): `channel`, `population`,
`well`, `parameter`, …
Joined from a sample sheet or plate layout.
Recorded in the file's own metadata (sample id, well, instrument).
A measured or computed value.
`error`, `error_code`.

SampleSheet.description: A sample sheet or plate layout in long form.

columns.description: Column names (a layout: `well`, then one per grid).

SheetKind.description: How the sheet was laid out.

oneOf.description: A header row, one row per sample.
Plate-shaped grids, one per annotation, turned into one row per well.

SummaryOutput.description: A summary: one row per group and value column.

control.description: The control group (value of the first `by` column).

group_by.description: Columns that define a group: `by` plus the measurement dimensions added.

rows_excluded.description: Rows left out by filters or errors.

rows_used.description: Table rows used / left out (errors, filters, missing values).

Table.description: A table: columns and rows of cells in column order.

rows.description: Rows; each has one cell per column.

oneOf.description: Comma-separated values with a header row.
Tab-separated values with a header row.
One JSON object per row and line.
Apache Parquet (Snappy), with column metadata.

anyOf.description: No value (JSON `null`, an empty CSV field).
A real number (NaN and infinities are written as `null`).

verified.description: Read back and checked before it was renamed into place.

columns.description:
Columns of `rows`, with type, unit and role (`id`, `key`, `metadata`, `annotation`,
`value`, `error`).

grain.description: Columns that identify a row within its data set.

inputs.description: How the inputs became data sets.

joins.description: Sample sheets and layouts joined, in order.

offset.description: Index of the first row in `rows`.

output.description: The file the full table was written to (`-o`).

rows.description: Rows as arrays in column order.

truncated.description:
True when the table has rows after the last one returned (page with `offset`, or read
the full table from `output`).

warnings.description: Things to check: skipped inputs, grouping, join results.
